extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and other submitters to the National Book Awards; the literary community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level requirements for works to be considered for the National Book Awards, including the categories honored, publication timing, eligibility/deadline procedures, and use of award medallions/rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although other categories have been recognized in the past, submissions should be for one of these current categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles honored are those ``published each year.''
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must be books published in the relevant awards year (see Deadlines & Guidelines for exact eligibility windows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope (American literature focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established to celebrate the best writing in America and are overseen by the National Book Foundation, whose mission is to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Awards emphasize the cultural value of American writing; consult Eligibility & Guidelines for specifics about who/what qualifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines & Guidelines (eligibility and submission process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines & Guidelines: Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must follow the published eligibility rules, adhere to submission deadlines, and comply with the stated procedures and prize rules (details available via the Read More link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and digital image rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners, finalists, and longlisted titles may use official seals/digital images; consult the Medallions page for usage rules and how to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special honors (5 Under 35 and Distinguished Contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to medallions for individual titles, there are medallions for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists, which can be used for future or backlist titles, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special honors recognize emerging writers (5 Under 35) and lifetime contributions; their medallions have distinct usage rules and applicability to future or backlist titles.
